finding: The completed merge profile locates the largest measured merge block in multi-branch value processing (17.830–21.302 instrumented CPU-seconds per active worker). About 19 million key visits must not be equated to exclusive combine time: that block includes lookups, equality, counters and nested combining. The retained partial Linux profile separately attributes 11.813 cumulative seconds to uncached _combine and 16.499 to combine; these overlap and have a different input/environment.
candidate_basis: Each active worker makes roughly 0.92–0.96 million combine_instances calls from merge, averaging 3.69–3.77 operands. Counts do not establish how many generic uncached combinations contain exactly two distinct object identities. Measure that before changing code.
source_semantics: The generic >2-operand path uses set unions, intersections and any/all reductions; its generated key uses sorted unique operand keys. After existing identical-value and missing/None handling, repeated references to the same immutable Value do not change those reductions. If precisely two distinct Value objects remain, the existing two-value branch computes the same fields and key. Keep original operand order for the pair, preserve explicit key overrides, and leave combine_instances alias side effects and the existing LRU cache in place.
risks: An extra identity scan and recursive cache lookup can cost more than they save.
The generic path may rarely contain exactly two distinct references.
Cache eviction changes may affect overall performance even with equivalent values.
None/missing, source-free guard stripping, every Value field, explicit/generated keys and instance side state require semantic controls.
